brief.summary: A shared house-guide app for families who co-own a vacation home, which pins every manual, shutoff, procedure and quirk to its actual place in the building and on the property so whoever arrives next knows where things are and how they work.

brief.moment: Ellen arrived Saturday afternoon, with a hard freeze forecast for Tuesday night. brief.data: Property: 'Sørby cabin, Ten Mile Lake, Hackensack MN', 2.3 acres. Buildings: main cabin (2 floors + crawlspace), guest bunkhouse, boathouse, woodshed, outhouse. Main cabin floor plans with 9 rooms. 46 pinned items, each placed at a location and carrying a type, title, notes, photo and attached document where relevant, e.g., 'Main water shutoff – red handle, left of pressure tank' (utility room), 'Well pump breaker #14' (panel in mudroom, 24-circuit panel with all circuits labeled), 'Bunkhouse drain valve' (north crawlspace hatch, 1.5 m in), 'Propane tank, 500 gal, Lakes Gas acct 88-2140' (east of driveway, 30 m from boathouse), 'Septic cleanout cap' (by the birch clump), 'Chimney damper lever'. 7 appliance manuals (Goulds well pump, Rheem water heater, Rinnai wall furnace, etc.). 'Fall closing' procedure, 22 steps, each tied to a pinned spot; Pete marked 4 steps 'changed 2025'. Notes from each sibling with dates; last closing by Pete Oct 19, 2025.

prompt:
I need the front end for Cabinbook. A shared house-guide app for families who co-own a vacation home, which pins every manual, shutoff, procedure and quirk to its actual place in the building and on the property so whoever arrives next knows where things are and how they work.

Who's using it: Ellen Sørby, 52, one of three siblings who inherited their parents' lakeside cabin in northern Minnesota. Her brother Pete usually opens the cabin each spring and closes it each fall, but this year Ellen is closing it alone for the first time in about eight years, with her teenage son helping.

What they're doing right now: Ellen arrived Saturday afternoon, with a hard freeze forecast for Tuesday night. She has to winterize: shut off and drain the water system, find the well pump breaker, blow out the lines to the outdoor shower, put antifreeze in the traps, turn the propane down at the tank, and close the chimney damper. She's standing in the utility room trying to figure out which of the two valves near the pressure tank is the main shutoff, where the drain-down valve for the guest bunkhouse is (Pete's note says 'under the north crawlspace hatch'), and where on the property the septic cleanout and the propane tank actually are relative to the boathouse.

What's in the system at this point: Property: 'Sørby cabin, Ten Mile Lake, Hackensack MN', 2.3 acres. Buildings: main cabin (2 floors + crawlspace), guest bunkhouse, boathouse, woodshed, outhouse. Main cabin floor plans with 9 rooms. 46 pinned items, each placed at a location and carrying a type, title, notes, photo and attached document where relevant, e.g., 'Main water shutoff – red handle, left of pressure tank' (utility room), 'Well pump breaker #14' (panel in mudroom, 24-circuit panel with all circuits labeled), 'Bunkhouse drain valve' (north crawlspace hatch, 1.5 m in), 'Propane tank, 500 gal, Lakes Gas acct 88-2140' (east of driveway, 30 m from boathouse), 'Septic cleanout cap' (by the birch clump), 'Chimney damper lever'. 7 appliance manuals (Goulds well pump, Rheem water heater, Rinnai wall furnace, etc.). 'Fall closing' procedure, 22 steps, each tied to a pinned spot; Pete marked 4 steps 'changed 2025'. Notes from each sibling with dates; last closing by Pete Oct 19, 2025.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
